question: What is the quation of line through (-1,-2) with slope -3.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The equation of a line passing through a given point must satisfy the coordinates of that point.

Substitute x = −1 and y = −2 in the given options to verify.

Option 1: −3(−1) − 5 = 3 − 5 = −2 (Satisfies the point)

Other options will not yield −2.

**∴ The correct answer is y = −3x − 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Coordinates of the point = (−1, −2)

Slope of the line (m) = −3

**Formula Used:**

The equation of a line passing through point (x₁, y₁) with slope m is given by: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

**Calculations:**

⇒ y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

⇒ y − (−2) = −3[x − (−1)]

⇒ y + 2 = −3(x + 1)

⇒ y + 2 = −3x − 3

⇒ y = −3x − 3 − 2

⇒ y = −3x − 5

**∴ The correct answer is y = −3x − 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slope-Intercept Form

The equation of a straight line with slope m and y-intercept c is given by the formula y = mx + c.

Two-Point Form

The equation of a line passing through two distinct points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is y − y₁ = [(y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁)](x − x₁).

Intercept Form

A line that has x-intercept a and y-intercept b on the coordinate axes follows the equation x/a + y/b = 1.
